note: The resolve1 shape, captured whole from the guest that runs resolved: the manager GetAll that doubles as the mode probe, GetLink for the one real interface, and the link's own GetAll — where the DHCP-provided server actually lives. The manager-level CurrentDNSServer is the empty struct (0,0,[]) and must be OMITTED, not rendered as an empty address; the server is homed on ifindex 2, so GlobalDNSServers is honestly empty while DNSServersInUse carries it from the link; and the link takes the DNS default route, so NoLinkTakesDNSDefaultRoute is false and the fallback rule must NOT fire. Two curations, each stated: only the resolver's own payloads are staged, because this variant serves nothing else; and the manager document is staged minus DNSSECNegativeTrustAnchors — a compiled-in constant list identical on every install, read by neither implementation, whose reversed-octet in-addr.arpa spellings read as public addresses to any detector honest about address shapes. One plant: the manager-level CurrentDNSServer is staged as the link's server — the state every resolved host reaches after its first query, which a freshly booted capture happened to predate; the empty-struct-must-be-omitted shape stays covered by the per-link walk's own empty members.
anchors_note: Staged truth transcribed by hand from the bus documents: the in-use list unions to exactly the link-homed server, the global list is empty because ifindex 2 is neither the classic global scope nor loopback, and the derived default-route fact is false because the walked link carries DefaultRoute true. The object is named for the captured host.
